content: The provided text appears to be a list of references formatted in a fragmented and non-standard way. 1. In 2015, a report was published detailing the global burden of healthcare-associated infections, emphasizing their endemic nature and the challenges they pose to healthcare systems worldwide. This report was accessed on October 18, 2016. 2. Allegranzi B, Bagheri Nejad S, Combescure C, Graafmans W, Attar H, Donaldson L, et al. conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis in 2011, published in The Lancet, which quantified the burden of endemic healthcare-associated infections in developing countries. The study highlighted the significant impact of these infections on patient outcomes and healthcare resources. 3. Shekelle PG, Pronovost PP, Wachter RM, McDonald KM, Schoelles K, Dy SM, et al. identified the top 10 patient safety strategies that could be implemented immediately to improve healthcare outcomes. This work was published in Annals of Internal Medicine in 2013. 4. The World Health Organization (WHO) released the second edition of its handbook for guideline development, which provides a comprehensive framework for creating evidence-based healthcare guidelines. This document was accessed on October 18, 2016. 5. Liberati A, Altman DG, Tetzlaff J, Mulrow C, Gotzsche PC, Ioannidis JP, et al. published the PRISMA statement in BMJ in 2009. This statement provides detailed guidance on reporting systematic reviews and meta-analyses of studies evaluating healthcare interventions. 6. Zingg W, Castro-Sanchez E, Secci FV, Edwards R, Drumright LN, Sevdalis N, et al. developed innovative tools for quality assessment, including the Integrated Quality Criteria for Review of Multiple Study Designs (ICROMS). Their findings were published in Public Health in 2016. 7. The Effective Practice and Organisation of Care (EPOC) group proposed suggested risk of bias criteria for EPOC reviews, providing resources for review authors. This framework was published by the Norwegian Knowledge Centre for the Health Services in 2015. 8. Balshem H, Helfand M, Schunemann HJ, Oxman AD, Kunz R, Brozek J, et al. outlined the GRADE guidelines for rating the quality of evidence in clinical research. This work was published in Journal of Clinical Epidemiology in 2011. 9. Guyatt G, Oxman AD, Akl EA, Kunz R, Vist G, Brozek J, et al. introduced the GRADE evidence profiles and summary of findings tables in their 2011 publication in Journal of Clinical Epidemiology. 10. Guyatt GH, Schunemann HJ, Djulbegovic B, Akl EA emphasized that guideline panels should not apply GRADE to good practice statements. This perspective was published in Journal of Clinical Epidemiology in 2015. 11. Guyatt GH, Alonso-Coello P, Schunemann HJ, Djulbegovic B, Nothacker M, Lange S, et al. provided guidance on the infrequent use of good practice statements by guideline panels, as outlined by the GRADE Working Group. This article was published in Journal of Clinical Epidemiology in 2016. 12. The third edition of the International Health Regulations (IHR) was published by the WHO, providing a framework for global health security. This document was accessed on October 18, 2016. 13. The WHO's IHR core capacity monitoring framework includes a checklist and indicators for tracking progress in developing IHR core capacities among State Parties. This resource was accessed on October 18, 2016. 14. The WHO's global strategy on integrated, people-centered health services for 2016–2026 was summarized in an executive summary, accessed on October 18, 2016. 15. The WHO published a framework for strengthening health systems to improve health outcomes, emphasizing the importance of coordinated action. This document was accessed on October 18, 2016. 16. Scott II RS highlighted the economic benefits of infection prevention in hospitals in a report accessed on October 18, 2016. 17. The European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control (ECDC) published its annual epidemiological report on communicable diseases in Europe in 2008, providing insights into the state of communicable diseases in EU and EEA/EFTA countries. 18. Graves N discussed the economics of preventing hospital-acquired infections in a 2004 article in Emerging Infectious Diseases. 19. Abad C, Fearday A, Safdar N conducted a systematic review in 2010, published in Journal of Hospital Infection, on the adverse effects of isolation on hospitalized patients. 20. The WHO published a report on water, sanitation, and hygiene in healthcare facilities, focusing on the status in lowand middle-income countries and strategies for improvement. This report was accessed on October 18, 2016. 21. The WHO released a report on the evolving threat of antimicrobial resistance and options for action, accessed on October 18, 2016. 22. The UK government outlined its five-year antimicrobial resistance strategy for 2013–2018, emphasizing the need for coordinated action to combat resistance. This strategy was accessed on October 18, 2016. 23. The WHO published guidelines on hand hygiene in healthcare as part of its First Global Patient Safety Challenge, emphasizing the importance of clean care for safer care. This document was accessed on October 18, 2016. 24. Haley RW, Culver DH, White JW, Morgan WM, Emori TG, Munn VP, et al. demonstrated the efficacy of infection surveillance and control programs in preventing nosocomial infections in U.S. hospitals in a 1985 study published in American Journal of Epidemiology. 25. Barsuk JH, Cohen ER, Feinglass J, McGaghie WC, Wayne DB showed that simulation-based education can reduce catheter-related bloodstream infections in a 2009 study published in Archives of Internal Medicine. 26. Numerous studies have demonstrated the effectiveness of education, feedback, and multidisciplinary approaches in improving hand hygiene compliance and reducing healthcare-associated infections across various settings, including intensive care units, emergency departments, and endoscopy units. These findings underscore the critical role of targeted interventions in infection prevention and control.
